cards.title: Tens that make 100
cards.body: $100$ is ten tens. So the bonds to $10$ give bonds to $100$ in tens: $3 + 7 = 10$, so $30 + 70 = 100$. The five tens bonds are $10 + 90$, $20 + 80$, $30 + 70$, $40 + 60$ and $50 + 50$.

cards.title: Worked example: what goes with 37?
cards.problem: What number goes with $37$ to make $100$?

steps.text: Start with the ones: $7$ needs $3$ to make a ten.
Those ones make a new ten, so the tens only need to make $9$, not $10$: $3$ tens need $6$ more tens.
So the answer is $63$. Check: $37 + 63 = 100$. The pattern: the tens make $9$ and the ones make $10$.
So $100 - 46 = 54$. No borrowing, no counting back: just two bonds.

cards.title: The common trap
cards.body: For $37$, some people answer $73$: they make the tens $10$ and the ones $10$. Check: $37 + 73 = 110$, one ten too many. The ones already make a ten, so the tens make $9$. Only a number that ends in $0$, like $40 + 60$, has tens that make $10$.

prompts: Why do the tens make $9$, and not $10$, in $37 + 63 = 100$?
